title: Anxious about the future
description: When worry about how things will turn out keeps you awake.

verses.note: Your part is the effort, not the outcome. Putting down the weight of results frees you to act well.
Steadiness in success and failure alike is itself called yoga: a calm you can practise, not just wish for.
Every hard feeling has a beginning and an end. Bear it patiently; it will pass.
For those who trust, what is lacking is provided and what is had is preserved.
The Gita's final reassurance: take refuge, and do not grieve.

title: Struggling with anger
description: When irritation turns into words or actions you later regret.

verses.note: Anger doesn't appear from nowhere. It grows from dwelling on things, then attachment, then frustrated desire.
The cost of anger: confusion, forgetfulness, and finally the loss of good judgement.
Desire and anger are two faces of one restless energy. Recognising that is the first step to mastering it.
Lust, anger and greed are called three gates to self-destruction. Close them early.
Freedom and peace lie close at hand for those who have loosened the grip of desire and anger.

title: Grieving a loss
description: When someone you love is gone, or something you held dear has ended.

verses.note: Krishna's first teaching meets Arjuna in his grief, and gently points beyond it.
As we pass through childhood, youth and age, the self passes on. The one we love is not simply lost.
The self is never born and never dies. What is essential in a person cannot be destroyed.
Like setting aside worn clothes for new ones: an image many have found comforting in loss.
Death comes to everything that is born. Accepting this softens the sharpest edge of grief.

title: Unsure what to do
description: When you are torn between paths: career, family, or conscience.

verses.note: The Gita begins with exactly this confusion. Arjuna admits he doesn't know, and asks for guidance.
Your own path, imperfectly walked, is better than someone else's walked perfectly.
When in doubt, act. Doing your duty is better than standing still.
Fulfilment comes through devotion to the work that is truly yours.
The Gita repeats the teaching near its close: follow your own nature, not another's.

title: Feeling afraid
description: When fear of failure, change or the unknown holds you back.

verses.note: Fearlessness heads the list of divine qualities. It is something we can cultivate.
No sincere effort on this path is wasted; even a little of it protects from great fear.
Many before you have freed themselves from attachment, fear and anger. It can be done.
The steady mind is not shaken by adversity, and is free from fear.
A promise to hold on to: the devoted never perish.

title: Feeling alone
description: When it seems no one understands, or no one is there.

verses.note: Whoever sees the divine everywhere is never separated from it, and it is never separated from them.
The divine is seated in the heart of every being, including yours, right now.
You carry the Lord within you, wherever you are.
The divine is equal to all and close to all who turn towards it with love.
Nothing grand is needed: a leaf, a flower, a little water offered with love is received.

title: Lacking motivation
description: When you can't find the energy to begin, or to keep going.

verses.note: Krishna's wake-up call: this weakness doesn't suit you. Stand up.
Lift yourself by your own effort. You can be your own best friend, or your own worst enemy.
Keep doing what needs doing, without clinging to the outcome, and you rise.
Balance in eating, rest, sleep and work is the foundation that makes steady effort possible.

title: A restless mind
description: When your thoughts race and you can't settle or focus.

verses.note: Even Arjuna found the mind as hard to hold as the wind. You are in good company.
Krishna agrees it is hard, and gives the method: steady practice and letting go.
Each time the mind wanders, gently bring it back. That returning is the practice.
Like a tortoise drawing in its limbs, withdraw the senses from what disturbs them.
Without a steady mind there is no peace, and without peace, no happiness.

title: Caught in craving
description: When wanting more, and never feeling it is enough, takes over.

verses.note: Desire is like fire: the more you feed it, the more it wants.
Pleasures that begin and end with the senses are a source of pain. The wise do not rest their happiness there.
Be like the ocean: rivers pour in, yet it stays full and unmoved.
Peace comes to the one who moves through life without craving or the sense of 'mine'.

title: Doubting yourself
description: When you feel unworthy, or weighed down by past mistakes.

verses.note: Even the greatest wrongdoer can cross over on the raft of knowledge. No one is beyond redemption.
What matters is the direction you now face, not where you have been.
Don't put yourself down. Raise yourself up; you can be your own friend.
When you have mastered yourself, your own mind becomes your ally.
Whatever is excellent in any being, including you, is a spark of the divine.

title: When ego gets in the way
description: When pride, the need to be right, or 'I did this' takes over.

verses.note: Nature does the work; only a mind confused by ego thinks 'I am the doer'.
Wisdom starts with humility, sincerity, patience and forgiveness.
Arrogance, conceit and harshness are named plainly, so we can recognise them in ourselves.
With a mind set on the divine you overcome every obstacle; ego alone leads to downfall.

title: Seeking inner peace
description: When you long for calm that doesn't depend on circumstances.

verses.note: Peace follows immediately upon letting go of the fruits of action.
Without hatred, friendly and compassionate to all, the same in joy and sorrow.
Neither troubling the world nor troubled by it, free from agitation, fear and anxiety.
Knowing the divine as the friend of all beings, one attains peace.
Letting go of craving and the sense of 'mine' is the doorway to peace.
